summary: Mun-keat Choong specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute, Komazawa University (BA), and the University of Queensland (MA and PhD), where he was supervised by Roderick S. Bucknell.

Munenobu Sakurai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral course at Tohoku University around 1986–1991, served as assistant professor at Iwate University (ca. 1994–2002), and became professor at Tohoku University around 2002.

Muneo Tokunaga was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kyoto University and Harvard University (PhD, ~1974–1979). He served as assistant professor at Tokyo Institute of Technology and Kyoto University, later becoming a professor at Kyoto University (~1995–2009).

Muneyoshi Yanagi was a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki around 1906–1910 and attended the University of Tokyo from around 1910 to 1913.

Mungunchimeg Batmunkh is a scholar in religious studies, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (attested 2010), where she studied under doctoral supervisor Brigitte Marschall.

Murray Barnson Emeneau was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Dalhousie, Oxford, and Yale under Franklin Edgerton, Edgar H. Sturtevant, and Edward Sapir. He taught Latin at Yale and served as professor of Sanskrit and linguistics at UC Berkeley (1940–1971).

Musashi Tachikawa, a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, studied at Nagoya University and Harvard (PhD, under Daniel H. H. Ingalls). His career included posts at Nagoya University, the National Museum of Ethnology, and Aichi Gakuin University.

Muzaffar Alam is a historian and scholar of Indology and Central Asian studies. After degrees at Jamia Millia Islamia, AMU, and JNU (doctorate), he taught at JNU (~1973–2001) before becoming a professor at the University of Chicago around 2001.

Myles Dillon was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at University College Dublin and under Rudolf Thurneysen, among others. He held posts at Trinity College Dublin, UCD, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and served as Director of DIAS (1960–1968).
Myokyo-ni was a Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at the University of Graz and trained under traditional teacher Sōkō Morinaga from around 1960 to 1972.
Myoshin Fujitake works in Buddhist studies. He has served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University and as a committee member at the Otani Academic Society (attested 2000).

Mysore Hiriyanna was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies who earned his BA and MA at Madras Christian College. He held posts at Maharaja's College, Mysore (1912–1927), and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Mysore (~1917–1927).

Akio Tatsuguchi (Myōsei Tatsuguchi) is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Diane E. Riggs and Jeff Wilson. He served as a professor (attested 1987) and later professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Ryukoku University.

Mónika Kiss works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. A PhD student in Japanese Studies at Eötvös Loránd University, she studied under advisor Masanori Yamaji as well as Robert F. Rhodes and Nozomu Saito.

N. A. Jayawickrama was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Professor at the University of Ceylon (~1958–1978) and at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1978–1985).
N. Aiyaswami Sastri was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held professorships at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (attested 1940) and Visva-Bharati University (attested 1971).
N. D. Mironov was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Leipzig University around 1902–1903 and studied under Hermann Jacobi and Heinrich Hübschmann.

N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Vice Chancellor of National Sanskrit University (1989–1994) and as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (~1989–2017).

N. Veezhinathan is an Indologist who earned his PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University under A. Sankaran. After research at Deccan College (1960–1963), he became Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1964, succeeding K. Kunjunni Raja.

N. Venkataramanayya was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who studied under Ferrand E. Corley. He served as Reader of Indian History and Archæology at the University of Madras and as Deputy Director for Epigraphy in Andhra Pradesh.
